questions.question: What two conditions must a list of vectors satisfy to be an eigenbasis?
options: It must span only the kernel of the operator.
It must be linearly dependent and contain one eigenvector.
It must contain every eigenvalue, and every vector must be zero.
It must be a basis, and every vector in the list must be an eigenvector.
questions.explanation: An eigenbasis is a basis of the space in which every vector is an eigenvector of the operator.
questions.source_support: Definition: an eigenbasis is a basis consisting entirely of eigenvectors of a linear operator.
questions.skill_detail: Recall the two-part meaning of eigenbasis.

A basis is linearly independent, not dependent.
Eigenvectors are nonzero; not every vector is zero.

A matrix with all entries equal

questions.explanation: A matrix is diagonalizable precisely when its eigenvectors span the whole space, i.e. they form a basis; in that eigenbasis each basis vector is scaled by its eigenvalue, so the matrix becomes diagonal.
